S18.01.note: The code sets the title to the first 40 characters of the first message (chat.tsx around line 762), with 'New chat' as fallback. No AI-generated summary title was found in apps/mobile; a server-side title step is unknown.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat by typing a first message and sending it.
Tap the Open menu button at the top of the chat, then tap See all chats.
Find the new chat's row in the list and read its title.
Compare the title with Expected: it should be a meaningful title without you naming the chat.
S18.01.where: Chat list row title of a new chat (Open menu > See all chats)

S18.02.note: The Conversation menu button is an icon with no visible text. Rename is also in the long-press menu on a chat row in See all chats.
steps: Open a chat that already has a title.
Tap the Conversation menu button (icon only, accessibility label 'Conversation menu') at the top of the chat.
Tap Rename.
Type a new name in the Rename chat box and tap Rename.
Leave the chat, open See all chats, and check the new name is still shown.
S18.02.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Rename

S18.03.note: The same Pin and Unpin items also appear in the Conversation menu inside a chat.
steps: Open Open menu > See all chats.
Long-press a chat row (or tap its More actions icon).
Tap Pin.
Check that the chat moves to the Pinned group at the top, and that the Pinned filter shows it.
Long-press the same row again and tap Unpin; check it returns to its date group.
S18.03.where: See all chats > long-press a chat row > Pin (or Unpin)

S18.04.needs: a signed-in account with a Cloud chat
S18.04.note: Archive is not offered for Local chats, per the code comment in useConversationActions.ts.
steps: Open a Cloud chat (archive is offered only for Cloud chats, not Local ones).
Tap Conversation menu and tap Archive.
Read the message 'Chat archived. Find it in Settings, Archived chats.' and check the chat is gone from See all chats.
Open Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Archived chats.
Tap Restore on the chat and check it comes back to See all chats.
S18.04.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Archive; restore at Settings > Privacy > Archived chats

S18.05.note: The Cloud text says the chat is removed from every device and can be restored from Recently deleted on the web; the Local text says it cannot be restored.
steps: Open a chat you are willing to delete.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Delete.
Read the Delete chat? box, which states what is lost, then tap Delete.
Check the chat is gone from See all chats and you are returned from the chat screen.
S18.05.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Delete

S18.07.note: Move to project is only offered when another project exists or the chat is already in one (canMove in the code).
steps: Open a chat that is not in a project.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Move to project.
In the Move to project list, tap a project name.
Check the toast 'Moved to <project name>' appears.
Open the project from the Projects tab and check the chat is listed there.
S18.07.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Move to project

S18.09.needs: a signed-in account whose plan includes AGI Work and Cloud mode; the switch is hidden on a chat that already started
S18.09.note: The switch only offers Chat and Work (not agent or plan), and it is hidden once the conversation has started, so changing the mode later in a chat is not shown in this control.
steps: Sign in on an account whose plan includes AGI Work, and start a new chat in Cloud mode.
Before sending anything, tap Work in the Chat or Work switch.
Send a message and check it is answered as planned, multi-step work with tools.
Send a second message and compare how it runs with Expected: later turns should follow the chosen mode.
S18.09.where: Chat tab > new chat > Chat or Work switch (Chat / Work)

S18.10.note: The same switch is also listed at Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Temporary Chat. The code stores it as a setting (isTemporaryChat), not per conversation.
steps: On the Chat tab, tap the eye-off button at the top right.
Read the Turn on temporary chat? box, which states the consequence.
Tap Cancel and check nothing changes; tap the button again and tap Turn on.
Check the button now shows the word Temporary.
Tap Temporary again to turn it off.
S18.10.where: Chat tab > top-right eye-off button (Enable temporary chat) > Turn on temporary chat?

S18.15.needs: a conversation long enough to scroll
S18.15.note: The button has no visible words; 'Scroll to bottom' is its accessibility label only.
steps: Open a chat with enough messages to scroll.
Scroll up several screens.
Look for the round button with a down chevron that appears over the thread.
Tap it and check the view jumps to the latest message and the button hides.
S18.15.where: Open a long chat > scroll up > round down-arrow button (Scroll to bottom)

S18.17.needs: a chat with messages; not available in temporary chats
S18.17.note: No tree view was found: each branch is a separate chat, and switching uses the Previous and Next arrows on alternate answers.
steps: Open a chat with at least one reply.
Long-press a message (about half a second).
Tap Branch Conversation from Here.
Check the toast 'Conversation branch created' and the new chat titled '<chat title> (branch)'.
For alternate answers, look for the Previous and Next arrows under a reply that has more than one version and tap them.
S18.17.where: Open a chat > long-press a message > Branch Conversation from Here

steps: Open a chat that has messages.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Export.
Read the Export Conversation list: Export as PDF, Print, Export as Text, Export as Markdown, Copy All Messages.
Tap Export as Markdown and choose where to save or share the file.
Open the file and check every message is in it, in order.
S18.18.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Export > Export as Markdown

labels.text: Share a link to this chat?

S18.19.needs: a signed-in account and a Cloud chat
S18.19.note: For a temporary chat the menu item is Share link and first asks Save this chat to share it?. The read-only check is not visible in the code, so it is only a tester check.
steps: Open a signed-in Cloud chat that is not temporary.
Tap Conversation menu and tap Share.
Read Share a link to this chat? and tap Create link.
Choose a app from the share sheet to send the link.
Open the link in a browser that is not signed in and check the chat can be read.
S18.19.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > Share

S18.20.needs: a Cloud account with at least one shared link
S18.20.note: Settings also has a separate Shared Links row (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx) that opens the same screen.
steps: Tap Open menu, then Settings, then Privacy.
Tap Shared links.
Find a link you created (S18.19), tap Revoke, and read Revoke this link?.
Tap Revoke again to confirm and check the link leaves the list.
Open the old link in a browser and check it no longer opens.
S18.20.where: Open menu > Settings > Privacy > Shared links

S18.22.note: The rows come from summarizeContext; the exact row names were not checked against Expected.
steps: Open a chat that has messages and some context.
Tap Conversation menu and tap What is in context.
Read the sheet: the model, the percent of context used, and the list of context rows.
Check the rows cover files, instructions, memory and the token budget as Expected asks.
Tap Close context details to close.
S18.22.where: Open a chat > Conversation menu > What is in context

S18.28.needs: two devices signed in to the same account
S18.28.note: The Code line pointed to code that moved; sync is in apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts and apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts. Cross-device behaviour needs a second device to test.
steps: On device A (signed in), start or open a Cloud chat and send a message.
On device B, signed in to the same account, tap Open menu and then See all chats.
Find the same chat under Recent chats and open it; check the messages from device A are there.
Send a reply on device B and check it appears on device A after sync.
S18.28.where: Second device: Open menu > See all chats > open the same chat
